Translating Gartner's Vision for PMM's Future

Sean Thomson attended Gartner Marketing Symposium and came back with six signals that every product marketer needs to understand.

By Chris O'Hara · June 2026 · 5 min read

When someone spends a week at Gartner Marketing Symposium and comes back with a coherent synthesis instead of a pile of slide photos, that's worth paying attention to.

Sean Thomson

Product Marketing Strategist, SAP
LinkedIn →

Sean Thomson is a Product Marketing Strategist at SAP with a track record of leading high-impact teams in technology-driven environments. He attended last week's Gartner Marketing Symposium and synthesized the key themes into something actionable for the PMM community.

Across sessions on AI, GTM transformation, customer growth, market intelligence, and CMO leadership, Sean identified a consistent pattern: PMM is evolving from a function focused on messaging and launches into a strategic GTM orchestration capability responsible for connecting market intelligence, commercialization, customer growth, and business decision-making.

The Six Signals

Here's what Sean flagged as the key takeaways for product marketers:

Signal 1

AI Transforms the Operating Model

Leading orgs are moving beyond AI-assisted content creation toward AI-enabled GTM orchestration. PMMs design and govern AI workflows, not just use AI tools.

Signal 2

Market Intel Goes Strategic

Competitive advantage shifts to insight generation, signal detection, and decision-making. The PMMs who matter connect trends to strategy.

Signal 3

PMM as GTM Orchestrator

Organizations are looking to PMM to align Product, Marketing, Sales, CS, and Ops around unified GTM strategy. Owning the connective tissue.

Signal 4

Customer Growth in Scope

Adoption, retention, expansion, advocacy — increasingly showing up in PMM OKRs. The job extends beyond acquisition.

Signal 5

COE Model Returns

Centralized standards + federated execution. Without governance, AI-generated content becomes a consistency nightmare.

Signal 6

Market Shaping, Not Just Execution

Successful CMOs shape customer preferences and anticipate market shifts — not just deliver marketing results.

Why This Matters

The through-line across all six signals is that PMM's scope is expanding — and that AI is the accelerant. The organizations that win will combine AI capabilities with strong market intelligence, customer insight, and commercialization excellence.

"AI won't replace PMM. It will elevate PMM into a more strategic role — if we're willing to evolve with it."
— Sean Thomson

Sean's synthesis reinforces the direction of our PMM Community strategy. The function that masters these capabilities becomes essential. The one that stays focused on launch checklists becomes a cost center.

That's a bigger job than most of us signed up for. It's also a more interesting one.
